title: Governing law in federal court: Erie
shortTitle: Governing law in federal court: Erie
summary: Erie addresses the law a federal court uses when adjudicating rights governed by state law. Federal jurisdiction alone does not authorize creation of a federal general common law to replace state rules of decision.
notes: The statement state substance and federal procedure is a starting description, not a sufficient test. Hanna explains why the source of the federal rule changes the analysis.

sections.How to work through the question: Identify the precise disputed rule and the competing federal source. If a valid federal statute or applicable Federal Rule governs, analyze its scope and authority. Otherwise use the assigned Erie line to consider state rights, likely forum incentives, and the relevant federal judicial interests.
